title: Cut out elements that don’t add value
principle: AI loves to add and rarely subtract. Over-explanation and decorative chrome read as generated. Restraint looks premium. Your job in polish is mostly deletion—push the model to take the risk of removing code.
procedure: Audit the screen: what still needs to be there for the user’s job?
Kill decorative noise—glows, random text highlights, unnecessary containers, redundant labels when imagery already communicates.
Prefer native / system controls over worse custom buttons and fields.
Ask the agent explicitly to simplify layout, remove gradients/glows, and aim for true minimalism.
examplePrompts:
Dial this calorie tracker back:

- Simplify the layout into an image-centric grid
- Get rid of gradients, glows, and unnecessary containers
- Aim for a truly minimalist aesthetic that feels Apple-native
- Prefer built-in iOS components over custom buttons and text fields that look worse
- Remove extra labels and empty space where the food images already communicate the content
Cut pass with job sentences: for every visible block, write one job. Delete any block without a job. Do not replace cuts with a new 3-card feature grid.
tips: Even when you ask for “clean, minimalist,” models still add pink glows, random color highlights, extra labels, and bad custom controls.
Putting less on screen often communicates more—attention isn’t diluted by clutter.
Deletion feels risky to next-token models; you must demand it.

workedExamples.title: Calorie tracker cut story
workedExamples.before: Asked for clean minimalism; still got pink glows, random text highlights, redundant labels beside food images, custom controls worse than native iOS.
workedExamples.after: Image-centric grid; gradients/glows/containers gone; Apple-native components; tighter type—opinionated, quieter, clearer.
workedExamples.body: Primary Deliver case in the Lenny essay. Models won’t delete riskily without an explicit push. Cite: Lenny.

workedExamples.title: This desk’s cut list
workedExamples.body: Ochre accents, marketing stage strips, dual CTA rows, badge-above-H1 removed in the App Desk pass—restraint as the taste bet. See docs/REDESIGN.md.

antiPatterns: Asking for “minimal” once, then accepting the still-decorated result.
Adding explanatory labels when imagery already communicates.
Custom controls that look worse than platform natives.
checklist: Every element has a job for the user’s task—or it’s gone.
No glow/gradient chrome without compositional reason.
Native/system controls preferred where custom is weaker.
A second pass asked specifically for deletion, not addition.
promptWhy: Bullet deletion asks (grid, kill glows, native iOS) force subtractive edits models avoid by default.
Job sentences make cutting mechanical; ban on replacement grid stops whack-a-mole slop.

provenance.statement: Design Catalog editorial synthesis of the cited public sources; contracts and decision paths are our implementation guidance, not quotations or author endorsements.

useWhen: What can be removed without making the task harder?
avoidWhen: Never remove labels, focus indicators, error explanations or source attribution for visual quiet.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Cut out elements that don’t add value” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
For each element:
1. Name the task or meaning it supports.
2. If none, remove it.
3. Keep semantics, attribution and feedback.
4. Repeat the original task; restore anything necessary.
acceptance: Remove one ornamental layer; complete the same task with keyboard and pointer; confirm the primary action and necessary context remain explicit.
Every element has a job for the user’s task—or it’s gone.
No glow/gradient chrome without compositional reason.
Native/system controls preferred where custom is weaker.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Each remaining element explains content, action or identity.

comparison.bad: Nested boxes, generic badges and repeated headings obscure the actual content.
comparison.good: A clear title, a useful sentence and a shared rule expose the content hierarchy.
comparison.impact: Each remaining element explains content, action or identity.
